subject: Audit ledger export clarification — Acme Therapeutics evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Rios <elena.rios@acmetherapeutics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmetherapeutics.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit ledger export — scope and format questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. Our SOC2 auditor has asked for a machine-readable export of admin activity and operator-level audit logs covering the last 12 months. A few specific questions we want to clarify before we map this to our evidence request: 

1) Event coverage — can you confirm which event types are included in the admin ledger (e.g., role/grant changes, API key creations/revocations, model deploys/versions, operator console actions, session token events, IP+geolocation for interactive sessions)?
2) Retention windows — what are the default retention periods for (a) admin/operator events, (b) session traces/ephemeral telemetry, and (c) long-term audit snapshots? Are custom retention windows available per-tenant?
3) Export formats — do you provide a daily JSONL snapshot + manifest, or near-real-time streaming (Kafka/Cloud PubSub)? For the export we need a schema example and a checksum process for chain-of-custody.
4) PII handling — are there built-in redaction options or hashing for user identifiers (email, usernames)?
5) Delivery options — SFTP, pre-signed S3, or signed transfer with attested manifest? If SFTP, what keys/handshake do you require?

If possible, could you send a small sample export (non-production, redacted) and a short checklist we can hand to our auditor (Mark Liu)? Our target is to include this evidence bundle in the control set by next Friday.

Appreciate it — Elena
Elena Rios

Subject: Re: Audit ledger export — scope and format questions

Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; Kimberly will follow with the technical export spec and handoff steps. I copied Ben for sampling/retention policy confirmation.

Summary answers (short):
- Event coverage: admin ledger includes role/grant events, API key lifecycle, model deploys & rollbacks, config changes, operator console actions (approve/deny), and operator-run jobs. Session traces (request-level telemetry) are captured but stored separately and can be included in a snapshot on request.
- Retention: default tenant retention is 365 days for admin/operator events, 90 days for session traces by default. We support custom retention windows for Enterprise/Private customers via policy flag (can be extended to multi-year under contract).
- Export formats: we offer three modes — (1) daily JSONL snapshot + signed manifest (recommended for audits), (2) on-demand incremental snapshot (delta since timestamp), and (3) streaming (Kafka or pub/sub) for live integrations. Manifests include HMAC + SHA256 checksums.
- PII handling: export schema supports per-field redaction and deterministic hashing (SHA256 with tenant salt) for identifiers. We can also apply field-level suppression on exported snapshots.
- Delivery: supported: pre-signed S3 (preferred), secure SFTP, or HTTPS push to an auditor endpoint. For SFTP we provide a public key fingerprint and require an SFTP username + GPG-encrypted manifest if requested.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly will attach the JSONL schema and a short sample manifest (non-prod redacted).
2) Please confirm preferred delivery method (S3 vs SFTP) and whether your auditor needs streaming access or static snapshots.
3) If you want a one-off 12-month snapshot, give us the earliest start date and we will provide an ETA for the handoff.

I attached the sample files (redacted) and a checklist for Mark.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Audit ledger export — technical spec and handover notes

Hi Elena, quick technical follow-up with specifics you can hand to Mark. I kept the JSON field names as in the attached schema.

What we log (non-exhaustive):
- event_type: ADMIN_ROLE_CHANGE, API_KEY_CREATE, API_KEY_REVOKE, MODEL_DEPLOY, MODEL_ROLLOUT, CONFIG_UPDATE, OPERATOR_ACTION (approve/reject), USER_LOGIN, SESSION_START, SESSION_END, PERMISSION_CHANGE
- event_ts (ISO 8601), actor_id (deterministically hashed optional), actor_role, target_resource, resource_id, request_id, request_lat_ms, client_ip, geo_country, tenant_id, change_summary

Retention & export modes:
- Default retention: admin/operator events = 365 days; session traces = 90 days.
- Enterprise extension: up to 7 years on archived snapshots (contracted).
- Export payloads: daily JSONL (newline-delimited JSON), manifest.txt with file checksums (SHA256) and HMAC signature. Incremental exports provide a sequence token for resumable pulls.

PII / redaction options:
- Deterministic hashing: SHA256(actor_id + tenant_salt) so auditor linkage is possible but raw emails removed.
- Field-level suppression profile: we can remove client_ip and geo if requested.

Delivery and handoff checklist (recommended):
1) Decide delivery: presigned S3 + IAM read policy OR SFTP user + public key.
2) Confirm retention window for export scope (we will snapshot events in that window).
3) Provide auditor SSH key (if SFTP) or S3 bucket ARN for pre-signed upload.
4) We will produce a manifest.txt with per-file SHA256 and an HMAC of the manifest using tenant KMS key.

SFTP specifics (if chosen):
- We expect a 4096-bit RSA public key; username format: acme_audit_{tenant}; preferred cipher list: aes256-ctr, hmac-sha2-512.
- We will include sftp_handover_notes.pdf with a sample command set for retrieval.

Estimated ETA: for a 12-month snapshot (approx. 6–12GB depending on tenant activity) we can deliver the export within 3 business days after kickoff and key exchange. Smaller/delimited windows are faster.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute handoff with Mark next week and run a test transfer.

- Kimberly Park
Principal Product Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
